# Introduction

Most Standardised MedDRA Queries (SMQs) are "simple": a case qualifies as soon
as **one** reported term is part of the narrow (or broad) search. These can be
derived in a single `derive_vars_query()` call, as shown in the
[OCCDS vignette](occds.html).

A handful of SMQs are **algorithmic**. For these, the broad search terms are
split into categories and a case only qualifies if a particular *combination*
of categories is present. The combination is evaluated **across the records of
a case**, so it cannot be resolved by looking at a single record in isolation.

This article shows how to derive such a query in two steps:

1. Use `create_query_data()` to set up one query per algorithm category, and
   `derive_vars_query()` to add them all to the dataset. Keeping one variable
   per category makes the derivation traceable --- a reviewer can see exactly
   which term contributed which category.
1. Use `derive_vars_joined()` to evaluate the algorithm across all records of a
   subject and derive the final query variable.

## The example algorithm

We use *Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)* as the example. Its algorithm combines the
narrow search with four categories of broad terms:

| Category | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Narrow | Core anaphylactic reaction terms |
| A | Broad terms specific enough to qualify on their own |
| B | Upper airway / respiratory |
| C | Angioedema / urticaria / pruritus / flush |
| D | Cardiovascular / hypotension |

A case qualifies if it includes either

* a **narrow** term **or** a term from **category A**; or
* a term from **category B** **and** a term from **category C**; or
* a term from **category D** **and** (a term from **category B** **or** a term
  from **category C**).

i.e. `A or (B and C) or (D and (B or C))`.

# Accessing the MedDRA Database {#get_terms}

The terms of an SMQ are read from the MedDRA database by a company-specific
function passed to the `get_terms_fun` argument of `create_query_data()` ---
admiral does not provide one, as the database layout is company-specific. See
`create_query_data()` for the interface this function has to implement.

For an algorithmic SMQ the function additionally has to be able to return a
single algorithm category. `basket_select()` accepts any number of *named*
arguments via `...`, which are passed on unchanged inside the `basket_select`
object, so the category can be requested with e.g.
`basket_select(..., algorithm_category = "B")`.

The function below stands in for the company function so that this article can
be run. It serves a small, made-up term list rather than the real SMQ --- MedDRA
is a licensed dictionary, so its content cannot be shipped here.

```{r}
# stand-in for the company MedDRA database
smq_anaphylaxis_db <- tribble(
  ~TERMCHAR,                   ~SCOPE,   ~ALGCAT,
  "ANAPHYLACTIC REACTION",     "NARROW", NA,
  "ANAPHYLACTIC SHOCK",        "NARROW", NA,
  "ANAPHYLACTOID REACTION",    "NARROW", NA,
  "CIRCULATORY COLLAPSE",      "BROAD",  "A",
  "SHOCK",                     "BROAD",  "A",
  "BRONCHOSPASM",              "BROAD",  "B",
  "DYSPNOEA",                  "BROAD",  "B",
  "STRIDOR",                   "BROAD",  "B",
  "WHEEZING",                  "BROAD",  "B",
  "ANGIOEDEMA",                "BROAD",  "C",
  "FLUSHING",                  "BROAD",  "C",
  "PRURITUS",                  "BROAD",  "C",
  "URTICARIA",                 "BROAD",  "C",
  "BLOOD PRESSURE DECREASED",  "BROAD",  "D",
  "HYPOTENSION",               "BROAD",  "D",
  "TACHYCARDIA",               "BROAD",  "D"
)

# stand-in for the company get_terms() function
get_terms <- function(basket_select, version, keep_id, temp_env) {
  terms <- smq_anaphylaxis_db

  # a narrow search returns the narrow terms only, a broad search returns all
  # terms of the SMQ
  if (basket_select$scope == "NARROW") {
    terms <- filter(terms, SCOPE == "NARROW")
  }

  # `algorithm_category` is passed in via the `...` argument of
  # `basket_select()` and restricts the terms to one algorithm category
  if (!is.null(basket_select$algorithm_category)) {
    terms <- filter(terms, !is.na(ALGCAT) & ALGCAT == basket_select$algorithm_category)
  }

  out <- transmute(
    terms,
    SRCVAR = "AEDECOD",
    TERMCHAR,
    GRPNAME = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)"
  )
  if (keep_id) {
    out <- mutate(out, GRPID = 20000021L)
  }
  out
}
```

# Set up the Queries Dataset {#queries}

Each part of the algorithm is defined by its own `query()` object:

* `SMQ01` is the SMQ itself, retrieved with a broad search. This is the
  standard narrow/broad retrieval the algorithm is applied on top of, and it
  creates `SMQ01NAM`, `SMQ01CD`, `SMQ01SC` and `SMQ01SCN`.
* `CQ01` to `CQ05` are the building blocks of the algorithm: the narrow terms
  and the four categories.

The building blocks are defined as *customized queries based on a basket*, i.e.
the `basket_select()` object is wrapped in a `list()`. That way only `CQzzNAM`
is created for them --- a plain `basket_select()` would additionally populate
`SCOPE`, giving non-standard `CQzzSC` variables which add nothing here, as the
scope is already captured by `SMQ01SC`.

```{r}
anaphylaxis_queries <- list(
  query(
    prefix = "SMQ01",
    name = auto,
    id = auto,
    add_scope_num = TRUE,
    definition = basket_select(
      name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
      scope = "BROAD",
      type = "smq"
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ01",
    name = "Anaphylaxis narrow terms",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "NARROW",
        type = "smq"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ02",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category A",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "A"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ03",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category B (upper airway/respiratory)",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "B"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ04",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category C (angioedema/urticaria/pruritus/flush)",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "C"
      )
    )
  ),
  query(
    prefix = "CQ05",
    name = "Anaphylaxis algorithm category D (cardiovascular/hypotension)",
    definition = list(
      basket_select(
        name = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
        scope = "BROAD",
        type = "smq",
        algorithm_category = "D"
      )
    )
  )
)

queries_anaphylaxis <- create_query_data(
  queries = anaphylaxis_queries,
  get_terms_fun = get_terms,
  version = "29.1"
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(queries_anaphylaxis)
```

# Example Input Data {#input}

```{r}
adae <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID, ~AESEQ, ~ASTDT,       ~AEDECOD,
  "01",     1,      "2021-03-05", "Anaphylactic reaction",
  "01",     2,      "2021-05-12", "Headache",
  "02",     1,      "2021-02-11", "Circulatory collapse",
  "03",     1,      "2021-04-02", "Dyspnoea",
  "03",     2,      "2021-04-02", "Urticaria",
  "04",     1,      "2021-06-18", "Hypotension",
  "04",     2,      "2021-06-18", "Wheezing",
  "05",     1,      "2021-07-21", "Hypotension",
  "06",     1,      "2021-08-03", "Urticaria",
  "06",     2,      "2021-08-04", "Pruritus",
  "07",     1,      "2021-09-09", "Nausea"
) %>%
  mutate(ASTDT = ymd(ASTDT))
```

# Step 1: Derive One Query Variable per Category {#step1}

A single `derive_vars_query()` call derives all prefixes at once.

```{r}
adae_query <- adae %>%
  derive_vars_query(dataset_queries = queries_anaphylaxis)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_query,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, SMQ01NAM, SMQ01SC,
    CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, CQ05NAM
  )
)
```

Note that none of these variables on their own answers whether the subject
qualifies for the algorithmic query: subject `03` has a category B term
(`CQ03NAM`) on one record and a category C term (`CQ04NAM`) on another.

# Step 2: Combine the Categories with `derive_vars_joined()` {#step2}

The algorithm is evaluated at case level, so each record of a subject needs to
"see" the other records of the same subject. This is what `derive_vars_joined()`
does: with `join_type = "all"` each record of the input dataset is joined with
**all** records of the same subject, and the joined variables are made available
with a `.join` suffix.

Because the condition has to hold across the whole case rather than for an
individual pair of records, `filter_join` uses the summary function `any()` ---
inside `filter_join` the joined dataset is grouped by the original observation,
so `any(!is.na(CQ03NAM.join))` reads as *"this subject has at least one category
B term"*.

```{r}
adae_alg <- adae_query %>%
  derive_vars_joined(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    order = exprs(AESEQ),
    mode = "first",
    join_vars = exprs(CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, CQ05NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join =
    # narrow term or category A
      any(!is.na(CQ01NAM.join)) | any(!is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) |
        # category B and category C
        (any(!is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) & any(!is.na(CQ04NAM.join))) |
        # category D and (category B or category C)
        (any(!is.na(CQ05NAM.join)) &
          (any(!is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) | any(!is.na(CQ04NAM.join)))),
    new_vars = exprs(SMQ02NAM = "Anaphylactic reaction (algorithmic)")
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, SMQ01NAM, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM,
    CQ05NAM, SMQ02NAM
  )
)
```

The `order`/`mode` arguments are required here only because more than one
record of the additional dataset satisfies the condition for a given input
record; since `new_vars` is a constant it does not matter which one is
selected.

Walking through the subjects:

* `01` qualifies on the narrow term *Anaphylactic reaction*. Both records of
  the subject are flagged, including the unrelated *Headache*, because the
  algorithm qualifies the **case**.
* `02` qualifies on the category A term *Circulatory collapse*.
* `03` qualifies on *Dyspnoea* (B) **and** *Urticaria* (C).
* `04` qualifies on *Hypotension* (D) **and** *Wheezing* (B).
* `05` has only a category D term and therefore does **not** qualify, even
  though it is part of the broad SMQ.
* `06` has two category C terms, which is not a qualifying combination.
* `07` is not part of the SMQ at all.

# Variations {#variations}

## Flagging only the contributing records

If the final variable should flag only the records which actually contribute to
the qualifying combination (rather than the whole case), drop the `any()` calls
and express the condition over the record pair instead. The current record's
variables are available unsuffixed and the joined record's with the `.join`
suffix:

```{r}
adae_alg_rec <- adae_query %>%
  derive_var_joined_exist_flag(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    order = exprs(AESEQ),
    new_var = ANAPTFL,
    join_vars = exprs(CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, CQ05NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join =
      !is.na(CQ01NAM) | !is.na(CQ02NAM) |
        (!is.na(CQ03NAM) & !is.na(CQ04NAM.join)) |
        (!is.na(CQ04NAM) & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) |
        (!is.na(CQ05NAM) & (!is.na(CQ03NAM.join) | !is.na(CQ04NAM.join))) |
        ((!is.na(CQ03NAM) | !is.na(CQ04NAM)) & !is.na(CQ05NAM.join))
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg_rec,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, CQ05NAM, ANAPTFL
  )
)
```

## Restricting the combination to a time window

The MedDRA algorithm is defined at case level, but a study may want to require
that the contributing events occur close to each other in time. Since the
joined dataset also exposes the dates, this is a matter of adding a condition on
`ASTDT` --- e.g. requiring the contributing terms to start within 7 days of each
other. Note that the window condition has to go **inside** each `any()`: placed
outside, it would be evaluated per record while the category check would still
look at the whole case.

```{r}
adae_alg_window <- adae_query %>%
  derive_vars_joined(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    order = exprs(AESEQ),
    mode = "first",
    join_vars = exprs(ASTDT, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, CQ05NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join =
      any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ01NAM.join)) |
        any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) |
        (any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) &
          any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ04NAM.join))) |
        (any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ05NAM.join)) &
          (any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) |
            any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ04NAM.join)))),
    new_vars = exprs(SMQ02NAM = "Anaphylactic reaction (algorithmic)")
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg_window,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, ASTDT, AEDECOD, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM,
    CQ05NAM, SMQ02NAM
  )
)
```

Subject `01` now only has its first record flagged: the *Headache* on
2021-05-12 is more than 7 days away from the anaphylactic reaction, so no
qualifying term is within its window.
